key_insight: Droplet charge and vertical electric fields can accelerate collision-driven cloud droplet growth, although their effects depend on charge polarity, droplet size, and field strength.
engineering_relevance: Electrostatic collision kernels could improve cloud microphysics models used to predict droplet growth and warm-rain initiation.
method: Compute droplet-pair trajectories with inertia, exact two-body Stokes hydrodynamics, electrostatic forces, and van der Waals forces.
Derive collision efficiencies and kernels across droplet sizes, charges, and vertical electric fields.
Solve the stochastic collection equation on a two-dimensional mass–charge grid using a flux method.
evidence_signal: Simulations show that increasing the field from 5×10⁴ to 3×10⁵ V/m can raise uncharged-pair collision efficiency tenfold for larger-droplet radii of 10 or 20 μm; by 40 minutes, every electrified case has a larger-radius large-droplet mode than the hydrodynamic reference.
watch_item: The model assumes spherical conducting droplets settling in still air under a uniform vertical field; applicability to turbulent clouds requires further evaluation.
paper_title: Electrostatic effects on settling cloud droplets: from pair collisions to size distribution evolution
